claim: A single CloudHSM cluster can contain up to 28 HSMs, subject to account service limits.
question: How many HSMs can one CloudHSM cluster hold?

qualifiers.condition: subject to account service limits; the quotas page may state a lower default

evidence.quote: A single CloudHSM Cluster can contain up to 28 HSMs, subject to account service limits.

claim: Besides the daily AWS backups, keys can be exported (wrapped) out of a CloudHSM cluster and stored on premises, as long as they were not generated as non-exportable.
question: Can you take keys out of a CloudHSM cluster?

evidence.quote: Keys can also be exported (“wrapped”) out of your cluster and stored on-premises as long as they were not generated as “non-exportable."

claim: AWS CloudHSM has a service level agreement (SLA).
question: Is there an SLA for AWS CloudHSM?

evidence.quote: Yes, you can find the service level agreement (SLA) for AWS CloudHSM here.

claim: You do not share CloudHSM resources with other customers: you get single-tenant access to the HSM, which is accessible only to you, although the underlying hardware may be shared.
question: Is a CloudHSM HSM shared with other AWS customers?

values.display: the HSM is accessible only to you

evidence.quote: As part of the service you receive single-tenant access to the HSM.
Underlying hardware may be shared with other customers, but the HSM is accessible only to you.

claim: CloudHSM has physical and logical tamper detection and response mechanisms that trigger key deletion (zeroization) of the hardware.
question: What happens if someone tampers with a CloudHSM HSM?

evidence.quote: AWS CloudHSM has both physical and logical tamper detection and response mechanisms that trigger key deletion (zeroization) of the hardware.

claim: HSMs lock out an admin or crypto officer after a fixed number of failed login attempts, and lock out a crypto user, who must then be unlocked by a CO or admin.
question: How does CloudHSM protect against brute-force logins?

values.display: must be unlocked by a CO or admin

evidence.quote: After a fixed number of unsuccessful attempts to access an HSM with admin or crypto officer (CO) credentials, the HSM will lock the admin/CO out.
Similarly, after a fixed number of unsuccessful attempts to access an HSM with crypto user (CU) credentials, the user will be locked out and must be unlocked by a CO or admin.

claim: If an HSM fails or loses network connectivity, it is replaced automatically.
question: What happens when a CloudHSM HSM fails?

values.display: the HSM will be automatically replaced

evidence.quote: If an HSM fails or loses network connectivity, the HSM will be automatically replaced.

claim: A cluster with a single HSM can lose keys created since the most recent daily backup; clusters with two or more HSMs, ideally in separate AZs, do not lose keys if one HSM fails.
question: Could you lose keys if a single CloudHSM HSM fails?

values.display: it is possible to lose keys
will not lose keys if a single HSM fails

evidence.quote: If your AWS CloudHSM Cluster only has a single HSM, yes it is possible to lose keys that were created since the most recent daily backup.
AWS CloudHSM Clusters with two or more HSMs, ideally in separate Availability Zones, will not lose keys if a single HSM fails.

claim: Amazon cannot recover your CloudHSM keys if you lose your HSM credentials, because it has no access to your keys or credentials.
question: Can AWS recover your CloudHSM keys if you lose your HSM credentials?

values.display: no way to recover your keys

evidence.quote: Amazon does not have access to your keys or credentials and therefore has no way to recover your keys if you lose your credentials.

claim: CloudHSM provides FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated HSMs.
question: Which FIPS level do CloudHSM HSMs meet?

evidence.quote: Yes, CloudHSM provides FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated HSMs.

note: See cloudhsm-faq-hsm2m-fips-140-3-level-3 for the newer hsm2m.medium type.

claim: AWS CloudHSM offers hsm2m.medium instances that are single-tenant and FIPS 140-3 Level 3 certified, and offers a non-FIPS mode for use cases outside the FIPS 140-3 restrictions.
question: Is AWS CloudHSM FIPS 140-3 certified?

evidence.quote: AWS CloudHSM offers hsm2m.medium instances that are standards-compliant, single-tenant, and FIPS 140-3 Level 3 certified.
For customers with use cases outside the restrictions of FIPS 140-3, AWS CloudHSM offers the option to run in non-FIPS mode.

note: hsm2m.medium arrived after mid-2022; numbers+changes lens dates it from CloudHSM document history.

claim: FIPS 140-2 Level 3 is a requirement of certain use cases, including document signing, payments, and operating as a public Certificate Authority for SSL certificates.

evidence.quote: FIPS 140-2 Level 3 is a requirement of certain use cases, including document signing, payments, or operating as a public Certificate Authority for SSL certificates.

claim: CloudHSM does not support Amazon RDS for Oracle TDE directly; to protect RDS data with keys generated and stored in a CloudHSM cluster, use AWS KMS with a custom key store.

claim: The CloudHSM API manages clusters and HSMs (create, modify, delete, status) but cannot access the contents of the HSM or modify its users, policies or other settings.
question: What can and cannot the CloudHSM API do?

values.display: cannot access the contents of the HSM

evidence.quote: You can create, modify, delete, and get the status of CloudHSM Clusters and HSMs.
The API cannot access the contents of the HSM or modify any users, policies, or other settings.

claim: All communication between the CloudHSM client and your HSM is encrypted end to end, and AWS cannot see or intercept it.
question: Does the CloudHSM client library give AWS access to your cluster?

values.display: AWS cannot see or intercept this communication

evidence.quote: All communication between the client and your HSM is encrypted end to end.
AWS cannot see or intercept this communication, and has no visibility into your cluster access credentials.

claim: CloudHSM has no scheduled maintenance windows, but AWS may need maintenance for upgrades or faulty hardware; you are responsible for architecting the cluster for high availability.
question: Does AWS CloudHSM have scheduled maintenance windows?

values.display: your responsibility to architect your cluster

evidence.quote: No, but AWS may need to conduct maintenance in the event of necessary upgrades or faulty hardware.
Please note it is your responsibility to architect your cluster for high availability.

claim: In CloudHSM, key rotation depends on your type of application and is a process you run, for example by creating a new key; for envelope encryption without an existing rotation tool and process, you need to create one.
question: How are keys rotated in AWS CloudHSM?

values.display: depend on your type of application
you will need to create one

evidence.quote: Your rotation strategy will depend on your type of application.
If you do not already have a key rotation tool and process in place, you will need to create one.

note: d113. The FAQ describes no automatic rotation feature for CloudHSM keys; contrast kms-faq-auto-rotation-90-to-2560-days.

claim: CloudHSM publishes CloudWatch metrics for clusters and individual HSMs, which you can read and alarm on.
question: How do you monitor CloudHSM HSMs?

evidence.quote: AWS CloudHSM publishes multiple Amazon CloudWatch metrics for CloudHSM Clusters and for individual HSMs.
